Some of them need to be under seal, and I have indicated this in the notification. There is one particular document, and that is item 23242, the schedule C to the Krnojelac indictment. It is tendered only for reference purpose, as the witness refers to this throughout his testimony to identify particular victims. It would be easier if that would just be admitted for reference purposes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you have any objection, Mr. Robinson?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think we admitted the pseudonym sheet already.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And there are some photo documentation which is referred to as 65 ter number 11289.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm not sure if that has been uploaded in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, it has been uploaded in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I couldn't see it. Could you check it now?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: At least the ones that are --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we upload it [overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, it's a huge documentation and only a few photos are --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I get the signal from Mr. Reid now. I take it there should be no problem, but in relation to 16183, I'm afraid whether the witness had said anything in relation to this document. All I can read from the transcript was just the witness was shown this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I thought he has commented on this, but we can, of course, show it to him now briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, let's do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, and it cannot be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can we please have 16183 on the screen. And it is an ICRC document.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Sir, if you look at this document, is it -- this relates to you. Don't read anything from it, in particular not the name. It's related to your detention time. Can you please comment on this? It's referring to, in particular, the details on Kula.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239
utterances.text: I have before me a certificate of the International Committee of the Red Cross, which speaks of the period of my detention in the camps in Foca and Kula. Is this enough for you? I can also tell you that there are some items that are not correct there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's sufficient, sir. We will admit it under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P3348, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, that concludes the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Other associated exhibits will be admit the and given numbers in due course and some should remain under seal, as indicated.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Sir, you will be further asked by Mr. Karadzic in his cross-examination. Yes, Mr. Karadzic, can you start?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, your Excellencies, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Have in mind the Chamber is of the view that at the moment three hours would be sufficient for your cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Not all today. I think seeing the witness looking at his watch he can be assured that he won't be here for another three hours today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We will adjourn at 7.00, sir, and then we will continue tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we may briefly go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we are now in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, while it's still fresh in our minds, I would like to clarify a couple of points from today's examination-in-chief. I would kindly ask you, and I'm also reminding myself, to make breaks between question and answer because everything we say is being interpreted and we speak the same language so it could present a problem.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239
utterances.text: I shall try.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: On page 79 of today's transcript, you said that you heard that the Serb side or some official said that the Serbs could not live with the Muslims. Did you say that indeed?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: As a member of the SDA and a member of the municipal board, were you familiar with negotiations that we had at the level of the republic and the level of the municipality, the negotiations between the SDS and the SDA?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239
utterances.text: Partially. I don't know which aspect interests you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Do you agree that the starting platform of the SDA and the SDS, when it came to preservation of Yugoslavia, was identical, and that that was the basis for our coalition? We wanted to topple the communist regime and to --

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239
utterances.text: In which period of time do you say that these political parties had these views?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Before the elections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If I could give you a tip, as to how you can put a pause between the question and answer, it's to watch the transcript, which is moving, and when it stops, it means Mr. Karadzic's question has been translated. And then when the transcript stops, then you can start answering. Bear that in mind. Thank you. Do you understand? Do you follow? Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I'm now referring to the period of time before the elections when we agreed on the post-elections coalition and when, on the 15th of January, we formed a joint assembly and joint government. Do you remember that the SDA and the SDS both supported the preservation of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239
utterances.text: Yes, in the sense that within Yugoslavia, there should also be Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Then it's not true, witness, that the Serbs did not want to live with the Muslims. The truth is that they didn't want to live with the Muslims outside of Yugoslavia in a single unitarian Bosnia dominated by Muslims; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239
utterances.text: That's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Didn't we ask you to remain with us in Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239
utterances.text: Yes. But not in the rump Yugoslavia. Don't forget, Mr. Karadzic, or rather, you know this full well, that there are three nations living in Bosnia and Herzegovina, Muslims, Serbs and Croats, and that all of them need to find their own space in the country where they live.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Do you remember that in June and July, there was a process underway of an agreement, historic agreement, between Muslims and Serbs, proposed by a man from Foca, Adil Zulfikarpasic, and professor of philosophy, Filipovic? It was also supported by Mr. Izetbegovic. For two months we spoke of how Serbs should give up on all regionalisations and that Muslims and Bosnia should remain in Yugoslavia even in the rump Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239
utterances.text: No. I don't remember any such agreement.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Should I conclude, then, that you do not know all that well some general facts about the politics in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239
utterances.text: It wasn't my primary focus, the politics. Something else was. However, I knew the basic principles that applied to Bosnia and Herzegovina once Slovenia seceded and then Croatia. There was a referendum and people stated in large numbers that they wanted to live in an independent sovereign Bosnia-Herzegovina with three constituent peoples, Muslims, Croats and Serbs, together with the others.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, I'm interested in knowing whether I should devote attention to your general statements, sweeping statements, when you say that the Serbs said that they couldn't live with the Muslims. Now, if we call upon you to remain in Yugoslavia with us, in any variant, then that is not true, it doesn't mean that we can't live with you, it's that you didn't want to live with us.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, no. What I said is a fact, and it was broadcast over the local radio station, Serbian radio station in Foca, that the time had come for the Serbs to settle accounts with the balijas once and for all, and that the Serbs would no longer allow their ribs to be broken. They will no longer allow their children to be circumcised, and that the things that the hodzas did would no longer be allowed. And that was broadcast over the radio.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Now, witness, do you know about the Islamic Declaration by Mr. Izetbegovic as being the basis for a future Bosnia, and do you agree that the introduction of sharia law would have been unavoidable under that declaration?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239
utterances.text: What declaration do you have in mind? What Islamic Declaration are you referring to? When it was written, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: It was written in 1970 and Mr. Izetbegovic was tried because of it in 1983, but he didn't want to give it up but published it again later when I said that he should renounce it publicly. So are there two Islamic Declarations or only one, the Islamic Declaration of Mr. Izetbegovic?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239
utterances.text: Yes, only one Islamic Declaration. He never wrote another one, a second Islamic Declaration, that you have just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Now, would you agree that Momcilo Mandic, on the 6th of January, 1992, was not the minister of justice in Republika Srpska but the assistant minister of the interior in the joint government, the joint ministry?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239
utterances.text: What date in January did you mention? What year was that?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The document that was put to you on page 81 of the transcript today bears the date of the 6th of January, 1992. And you identified the collocutor, or rather, co-signatory, or rather, the person that was mentioned that it was the minister of justice in Republika Srpska. Now, do you agree that on the 6th of January, 1992, Republika Srpska was not in existence so he was the assistant of the minister for crime in the joint government?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239
utterances.text: No, I can't confirm that. I think he occupied the post that I stated earlier on.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, would you agree -- you say -- you mentioned the 20th of December or somewhere thereabouts, that the Serbian Ministry of -- municipality of Foca was constituted. Do you agree that it was just proclaimed but came into existence and started working only in April 1992? Would that be right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239
utterances.text: Let's go back for a moment to the date when the joint multi-party assembly was constituted, of the Muslims and Serbs, because they were the two leading ethnic groups in Foca, and that was the 25th of December, 1990. A year after that date it says over there -- or we see that the Serbian Municipality of Foca was constituted. So the date is the same but it's one year later, with all its bodies and organs.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And would it be true that this joint municipality continued to work and function right up to the 6th or 7th of April?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239
utterances.text: Yes. In formal terms, but objectively speaking, this did not happen because there was constant obstruction by the Serb representatives in the municipal authorities and agencies, and they carried out these obstructions quite consciously, and this served the Serbian Democratic Party to arm itself and prepare itself for an aggression because unfortunately that's what happened. There was an aggression in April and May in Bosnia-Herzegovina in a large number of municipalities during those two months. And that is something that only a people who had a lot of weapons could have carried out.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, may I ask you to stick to what you know 100 per cent, what you witnessed yourself. Now, tell me this: This meeting in Gorazde that you say Mr. Vojislav Maksimovic, a university professor, a member of the academy of science said that Cehotina would flow bloody, was that make meeting a public rally?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239
utterances.text: Yes, it was a public rally of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Was it the pre-electoral meeting?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure whether it was representing the SDS parties or whether it was the pre-electoral meeting because there were two rounds; first of all, in Bosnia-Herzegovina you presented yourself to the people as a party, and then the pre-election campaign started up.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, do you know that Mr. Vojislav Maksimovic, although he was on the list, he wasn't a member of the SDS right up until the spring of 1991, although he was on that ticket, but before that he was not in the party, he was president of the cultural society called Prosveta?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239
utterances.text: No, I don't know about that and I doubt what you're saying.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Very well. Now, what you're saying, that this eminent professor - and you say he was a distinguished professor - this drastic sentence of his, did anybody publish that, publicise that?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239
utterances.text: Well, yes, the media did. It was in the media.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Well, can you help the Prosecution out and get us a copy of that?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239
utterances.text: Well, it's up to the Prosecution to do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, on page 86 of today's transcript, mention was made of work obligations. Do you agree that a work obligation is something that was prescribed by law, the law on total national defence and social self protection, and that when there is imminent danger of war, those who are not up at the front must do something, do some work, and the local authorities decided what the work obligation would be?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239
utterances.text: That was what it was like in the previous system, and I can't remember that this document existed in the multi-party system.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: However, do you remember that all the laws that existed in the old Yugoslavia in the SFRY, and were not changed and they continued to be in force, so there was no legal vacuum so to speak?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239
utterances.text: Yes, that's true, most of them did continue to live on.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, can you tell us what was the army into which on the 8th of May Mr. Miro Stanic was commander of the tactical group of Foca? What army was that? The tactical group Foca, what army was that in, part of?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239
utterances.text: They had an army, that is to say they set up the Crisis Staff, and they recruited people from the SDS, from your party, and these people were called, referred to, as the Serb territorials to begin with.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, do you know when the Army of Republika Srpska came into being, of which I was the Supreme Commander, or rather the Presidency?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239
utterances.text: I think that was in May 1992. I'm sorry, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: 1991, you say?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Very well. You're probably tired. It was 1992 when the decision was made and then the army was formed afterwards. How could it have been in 1991 when we still had a joint state?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karadzic, we have the attack by the Serb forces at the beginning of April. Let me explain the situation to the Prosecution. First of all, there was the Territorial Defence, and then from the Territorial Defence -- or rather, it was transformed to become the Army of Republika Srpska. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Just as from the Territorial Defence of the Muslim forces and Croatian forces, the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina was formed, right, in similar fashion?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Now, on the 8th of May, 1992, yes, the 8th of May, 1992, would you agree that the Territorial Defence, by law, the law governing total national defence and social self protection, was a formation which belonged to the municipality, and the president of the municipality was the political leader, the Supreme Commander, of that unit which was -- had this municipal character?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, that was the case in previous documents. That's what was stipulated there. But let me remind you that in Foca, and the population of Foca already in May had been expelled -- it says in the reports that the Serb forces took control of the whole of Foca municipality by the end -- already by the end of April, and were moving towards Gorazde, whereas your -- you mention the 8th of May.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, let's clear this matter up. When you say Serb forces, do you mean that they were forces composed of Serbs, or do you consider that to be the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239
utterances.text: Well, I mean it to be the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And the Army of Republika Srpska, did it exist before the 20th of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239
utterances.text: Well, all right, Mr. Karadzic, we are just confusing the two. The Territorial Defence became the Army of Republika Srpska. This is just a formal transformation. And the role of your Territorial Defence, or as they were often referred to as the Serb territorials, it's the same thing, the same thing as the Army of Republika Srpska as it became known later on. And that's what it says in the Crisis Staff documents as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, witness, just a little patience. Legally speaking, we have to determine whether the Law on Total National Defence was changed or was the Territorial Defence the army of each municipality until it was changed, and the president of the municipality, by ex officio, was the president of the National Defence council, and the commander of the Territorial Defence was his tactical commander?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239
utterances.text: Well, I can't con firm that.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can you deny it, then?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239
utterances.text: I would be closer to denying it than to confirming it because according to the previous system, and the documents in the previous system is one thing, and as soon as the municipal assembly of Foca was formed, the Serbs carried out an obstruction. They failed to adopt an agenda, nothing could get done, the whole system was paralysed. So you're going very far away in saying that the Territorial Defence as a joint structure had been established.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know when the Crisis Staff of the SDA was formed and when the SDS Crisis Staff was set up?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239
utterances.text: My answer would be that I don't know that exactly. I don't know when the Crisis Staff was set up. I was wondering that when I was captured. Now, in your document, it says quite decidedly that the Crisis Staff was formed on 3 April and that it was composed of 15 members. Perhaps we could demonstrate that and have it shown on our screens.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, tell us, please, how many arrested Muslims were there in April, in the month of April, in those clashes? How many Muslims were arrested?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239
utterances.text: Well, the figure we arrived at was that in the KP Dom of Foca there were between 600 and 650 civilians incarcerated.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you. And how many Muslims lived in Foca municipality?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239
utterances.text: The number of Muslims was about 21,500 or 52 per cent of the population.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you. And you don't know why you were arrested although you were questioned? What were you questioned about?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239
utterances.text: I was interrogated formally. I was asked whether I had any weapons, nothing more than that.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You said a moment ago that you were asked when the Crisis Staff was established. Were there any other questions?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-239
utterances.text: The group that captured me asked me that, but the police later on, the police that came to the KP Dom to interrogate the prisoners, just asked me whether I was in possession of any weapons, and before that they had searched my flat. So it was just an official matter to call me in for an interrogation. They already knew that I didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Karadzic, and Mr. Witness, we will stop here and continue tomorrow morning at 9.00. In the meantime, while you are giving your evidence, you are not supposed to discuss about your testimony with anybody else. Do you understand that, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Please have a nice evening. 9.00 tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 16th day of September 2011, at 9.00 a.m. 25
